findings.title: POST /auth/logout accepts request with no Authorization header
findings.description: The endpoint POST /auth/logout returned HTTP 200 when called with no Authorization header. Authentication should be enforced and return 401 for all unauthenticated requests.
findings.suggested_fix: Return HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate header when credentials are missing or invalid.

findings.title: IDOR: carol can edit bob's post
findings.description: Carol sent PATCH /posts/374 (owned by bob) and received HTTP 200. The server should verify the authenticated user owns the post before allowing edits.
findings.reproduction: curl -X PATCH https://backend-agent-test.onrender.com/posts/374 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <carol_token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"body": "Overwritten by carol"}'
findings.suggested_fix: Check post.author_id == current_user.id before allowing PATCH.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Negative limit accepted without validation error
findings.description: GET /posts with limit=-1 returned HTTP 500. Invalid pagination values should be rejected.
findings.expected: HTTP 422 or clamped to 0 — negative limit is nonsensical
findings.suggested_fix: Add ge=0 constraints to limit and offset parameters.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Negative offset accepted without validation error
findings.description: GET /posts with offset=-1 returned HTTP 200. Invalid pagination values should be rejected.
findings.expected: HTTP 422 or clamped to 0 — negative offset is nonsensical
findings.suggested_fix: Add ge=0 constraints to limit and offset parameters.

findings.title: Uncapped pagination: limit=999999 returns oversized payload
findings.description: GET /posts?limit=999999 returned HTTP 200 with a 67,224-byte response body. There is no upper bound enforced on the limit parameter, which can be used to exhaust server and client memory.

findings.expected: HTTP 422 or response capped at a maximum page size (e.g. 100)
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce a maximum value (e.g. le=100) on the limit parameter.

findings.title: Non-integer path param not rejected: PATCH /posts/not-an-int
findings.description: PATCH /posts/not-an-int with a non-integer path parameter returned HTTP 401 instead of 422. Path parameters typed as integer in the spec should be validated before reaching business logic.
findings.expected: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity or 404 Not Found
findings.suggested_fix: Declare path parameter types as integer in the router; reject non-integer values automatically.

findings.title: Non-integer path param not rejected: DELETE /posts/not-an-int
findings.description: DELETE /posts/not-an-int with a non-integer path parameter returned HTTP 401 instead of 422. Path parameters typed as integer in the spec should be validated before reaching business logic.
findings.expected: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity or 404 Not Found
findings.suggested_fix: Declare path parameter types as integer in the router; reject non-integer values automatically.

findings.title: Unlike a never-liked post returns success silently
findings.description: DELETE /posts/374/like as carol returned HTTP 200 even though carol never liked this post.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 404 when the like relationship does not exist.

findings.title: Double-delete post returns success on already-deleted resource
findings.description: Deleting post 376 twice returned HTTP 200 on the second attempt. The post no longer exists so the server should return 404.
findings.expected: HTTP 404 Not Found on second delete
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the post exists before deleting and return 404 if absent.

findings.title: Ghost resource returns unexpected status: Comment on nonexistent post
findings.description: POST /posts/999999999/comments returned HTTP 401 for a nonexistent resource ID (999999999). Expected HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 404 for all references to nonexistent resource IDs.

findings.title: Ghost resource returns unexpected status: Like a nonexistent post
findings.description: POST /posts/999999999/like returned HTTP 401 for a nonexistent resource ID (999999999). Expected HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 404 for all references to nonexistent resource IDs.

findings.title: Ghost resource returns unexpected status: Follow a nonexistent user
findings.description: POST /users/999999999/follow returned HTTP 401 for a nonexistent resource ID (999999999). Expected HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 404 for all references to nonexistent resource IDs.

findings.title: Malformed JSON body leaks internals on POST /auth/login
findings.description: POST /auth/login with malformed JSON body returned HTTP 500. Traceback signals found: ['Internal Server Error'].
findings.expected: HTTP 400 or 422 with a clean JSON error message
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap JSON parse errors in a global exception handler that returns a clean 400/422 response without leaking internals.

findings.title: Missing security header: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.description: The response does not include the X-Content-Type-Options header. Without this header, browsers may MIME-sniff responses, enabling content injection attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to all responses.

findings.title: Missing security header: X-Frame-Options
findings.description: The response does not include the X-Frame-Options header. This can allow the API to be embedded in iframes, enabling clickjacking attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' to all responses.

findings.title: Missing security header: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
findings.description: The API does not send a Strict-Transport-Security header. As this is an HTTPS API, HSTS should be enforced to prevent protocol downgrade and cookie hijacking attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add HSTS header with a max-age of at least 1 year.

findings.title: CORS: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is wildcard (*)
findings.description: The API responds to cross-origin requests with 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *', allowing any origin to make browser-based requests. For an API accepting credentials this is overly permissive.
findings.expected: Specific allowed origin or no ACAO header
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict CORS to a whitelist of known origins. Never use wildcard when credentials are involved.

findings.title: CORS: Wildcard origin combined with Allow-Credentials: true
findings.description: The API sets both 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This combination is rejected by browsers (for security) but indicates a misconfigured CORS policy that could be exploited with non-standard clients.
findings.expected: Credentials must only be allowed for specific, trusted origins
findings.suggested_fix: Never combine wildcard origin with Allow-Credentials: true. Use an explicit origin whitelist.

findings.title: No rate limiting on POST /auth/login (15 requests, no 429)
findings.description: Fired 15 consecutive failed login attempts against POST /auth/login. All returned HTTP 401 without any throttling, delay, lockout, or HTTP 429 response. This endpoint is vulnerable to credential stuffing and brute-force attacks.
findings.reproduction:
for i in $(seq 1 15); do
  curl -X POST https://backend-agent-test.onrender.com/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"alice","password":"WRONG"}'
done
findings.expected: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests after repeated failures
findings.actual: All 15 requests returned 401 with no throttling. Status code distribution: {401: 15}
findings.suggested_fix: Implement rate limiting on /auth/login using IP-based or username-based throttling (e.g. max 5 failures per minute). Consider account lockout after N consecutive failures.

findings.title: No rate limiting on POST /auth/register (15 requests, no 429)
findings.description: Fired 15 registration requests against POST /auth/register. 15 succeeded with no throttling or 429 response. Without rate limiting, this endpoint enables account spam, resource exhaustion, and enumeration attacks.
findings.reproduction:
for i in $(seq 1 15); do
  curl -X POST https://backend-agent-test.onrender.com/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"spam_$i","password":"pass","email":"spam_$i@x.com"}'
done
findings.expected: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests after repeated registration attempts
findings.suggested_fix: Apply IP-based rate limiting to POST /auth/register (e.g. max 3 registrations per IP per hour).

findings.title: OPTIONS /posts returned 405, expected 200/204
findings.description: HTTP OPTIONS requests to /posts should return 200 or 204 with an Allow header listing supported methods. Got HTTP 405 instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure your framework to respond to OPTIONS requests properly.

findings.title: OPTIONS /users/me returned 405, expected 200/204
findings.description: HTTP OPTIONS requests to /users/me should return 200 or 204 with an Allow header listing supported methods. Got HTTP 405 instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure your framework to respond to OPTIONS requests properly.

findings.title: OPTIONS /auth/login returned 405, expected 200/204
findings.description: HTTP OPTIONS requests to /auth/login should return 200 or 204 with an Allow header listing supported methods. Got HTTP 405 instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure your framework to respond to OPTIONS requests properly.

findings.title: HEAD /posts returns 405 Method Not Allowed
findings.description: HEAD requests to /posts returned 405. HEAD should be supported on any GET endpoint — it returns the same headers without a response body, useful for caching and content negotiation.
findings.suggested_fix: Most frameworks support HEAD automatically for GET routes; verify it is not explicitly blocked.

findings.title: HEAD /posts/2 returns 405 Method Not Allowed
findings.description: HEAD requests to /posts/2 returned 405. HEAD should be supported on any GET endpoint — it returns the same headers without a response body, useful for caching and content negotiation.
findings.suggested_fix: Most frameworks support HEAD automatically for GET routes; verify it is not explicitly blocked.

findings.title: Empty request body causes HTTP 500 on POST /auth/login
findings.description: POST /auth/login with a completely empty body (0 bytes) returned HTTP 500. An empty body should return 400 or 422.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle empty bodies with a 400 or 422 response.

findings.title: Trailing slash inconsistency: /posts vs /posts/ return different status codes
findings.description: GET /posts → HTTP 200, GET /posts/ → HTTP 307. Trailing slash handling should be consistent; ideally one redirects to the other (301) or both return the same status.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure consistent trailing-slash handling (redirect or normalise at router level).

findings.title: Inconsistent post shape between feed and single-post endpoints
findings.description: GET /posts (feed) and GET /posts/{id} return different sets of fields for post objects. Only in feed: {'author'}. Only in single: {'authorName'}.
findings.expected: Same post object shape on both endpoints
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same post serialiser for both the feed and the single-post endpoint.

findings.title: Missing Cache-Control header on GET /posts
findings.description: GET /posts does not include a Cache-Control header. Without caching directives, clients and proxies cannot cache responses, causing unnecessary repeated requests to the server.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Cache-Control headers to public read endpoints. For frequently-changing feeds use short max-age (30–60s). For stable resources use longer max-age with ETag revalidation.

findings.title: Missing ETag and Last-Modified on GET /posts
findings.description: GET /posts provides no ETag or Last-Modified header. These headers enable conditional requests (If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since), allowing clients to avoid re-downloading unchanged content.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ETag headers (content hash) or Last-Modified (timestamp) to enable client-side conditional GET requests.

findings.title: Spec drift: Authorization header marked required:false but endpoint enforces auth
findings.description: The OpenAPI spec marks the Authorization header as 'required: false' on GET /users/me (and other protected endpoints). However, calling the endpoint without a token returns HTTP 401, proving auth IS required. The spec does not accurately document the authentication requirement.
findings.expected: Spec should declare Authorization as required:true or use a security scheme
findings.actual: Spec says required:false, but API returns HTTP 401 without auth
findings.suggested_fix: Use OpenAPI security schemes (BearerAuth) instead of manually declaring the Authorization header as a parameter. Mark the security scheme as required on protected operations.
